Most buyers spend all their time negotiating price.

The best buyers spend their time negotiating structure.

Because the right deal structure can create more value than a lower purchase price ever will.

Price is important.

Structure determines outcomes.

This is where many acquisitions succeed or fail.

Here's what disciplined buyers focus on:

Use the right financing mix

Most acquisitions are funded with a combination of SBA debt, seller financing, and equity.

The goal isn't to maximize leverage.

The goal is to create a structure the business can comfortably support.

Align seller incentives

Seller notes and earnouts can help bridge valuation gaps and reduce risk.

When both parties have something at stake after closing, interests stay aligned.

Negotiate terms, not just price

Purchase price gets the attention.

Terms create the flexibility.

Transition support, working capital, payment timing, and contingencies often matter just as much as the headline number.

Understand the lender's perspective

Lenders don't underwrite opportunity.

They underwrite risk.

The more lender-friendly your structure is, the easier it becomes to secure financing and close the deal.

Plan for cash flow first

Debt service doesn't care about your projections.

Build a structure that works during difficult months, not just good ones.

Protect the downside

The best buyers aren't trying to maximize returns at all costs.

They're building structures that preserve capital, reduce risk, and keep them in the game long enough to compound results.

My advice:

Don't ask how much business you can afford to buy.

Ask what structure gives the business the highest probability of success after closing.

Great acquisitions aren't built on aggressive assumptions.

They're built on disciplined financing, aligned incentives, and structures that work in the real world.

Как меняется наше время?
Вот несколько признаков новой реальности.

Многие чувствуют изменения, но не всегда могут объяснить, что именно происходит.

А ведь правила игры действительно меняются.

📌 Первый признак.

Труд обесценивается быстрее, чем растут навыки.

Раньше схема была простой:
учёба → работа → стаж → пенсия.

Сегодня всё иначе.

Технологии развиваются настолько быстро, что многие профессии меняются буквально на глазах.

Человек может работать больше, чем когда-либо раньше, но это уже не гарантирует финансового спокойствия.

📌 Второй признак.

Собственность постепенно уступает место доступу. Мы всё чаще арендуем, подписываемся, пользуемся. Музыка по подписке. Фильмы по подписке. Программы по подписке. Даже транспорт всё чаще не покупают, а используют по мере необходимости.

Мир движется от владения к доступу.

📌 Третий признак.

Самым ценным ресурсом становятся данные. Сегодня крупнейшие компании мира зарабатывают не только на товарах. Они зарабатывают на информации. На привычках. На поведении. На внимании. На прогнозировании решений людей.

Что всё это означает для обычного человека?

Очень простую вещь.
Старые финансовые модели постепенно перестают работать так эффективно, как раньше.
Уже недостаточно просто работать больше.
Важно учиться создавать активы.
Осваивать новые инструменты.
Развивать финансовое мышление.
Формировать дополнительные источники поступления средств.

Мир меняется независимо от нашего желания, но у каждого из нас остаётся выбор- наблюдать за изменениями со стороны или учиться использовать новые возможности себе во благо.

Через несколько лет разница между людьми будет определяться не тем, сколько часов они работают.

А тем, насколько быстро они смогли адаптироваться к новым правилам игры.

In reality, it's often determined by what you do with the money you make.

Two people can earn the exact same income and end up with completely different financial futures.

Because of how they think.

When money comes in, it goes right back out.

New clothes.

New gadgets.

New cars.

New upgrades.

The problem isn't spending money.

The problem is spending money on things that don't produce a return.

Money leaves and never comes back.

---

Saving money is important.

Everyone should have an emergency fund and financial reserves.

But saving alone rarely creates wealth.

Money sitting in a bank account is safe.

But it's not working.

It's waiting.

---

### The Wealthy Invest Money

The wealthy understand one simple principle:

**Money should have a job.**

Instead of asking:

*"What can I buy?"*

They ask:

*"What can I invest in?"*

They buy:

✔ Businesses

✔ Real Estate

✔ Stocks

✔ Cash-Flowing Assets

✔ Income-Producing Systems

Their money goes to work so they don't have to work forever.

---

### The Real Difference

The difference isn't how much you make.

It's what you do with what you make.

A person earning $60,000 who consistently invests can build more wealth than someone earning $250,000 who spends everything they make.

Income matters.

But habits matter more.

---

### Think About This

The next time money hits your account, ask yourself:

Will this purchase make me richer next year?

Or will it simply make me feel richer today?

That one question can change your financial future.

---

### Final Thought

The poor spend money.

The middle class save money.

The wealthy invest money.

The wealthy aren't focused on looking rich.

They're focused on building assets that create freedom.

Because true wealth isn't measured by what you own.

# THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN HOW THE WEALTHY THINK ABOUT MONEY

Most people work for money.

Wealthy people make money work for them.

The average person gets paid and buys:

• New Cars

• Designer Clothes

• Expensive Watches

• Electronics

• Vacations

None of those things put money back in their pocket.

They consume cash.

They're liabilities.

---

## Wealthy People Think Differently

When money comes in, they ask:

**"How can I turn this into an asset?"**

Instead of buying things that lose value, they buy things that have the potential to produce income.

Examples:

✔ Businesses

✔ Real Estate

✔ Stocks

✔ Cash-Flowing Assets

✔ Income-Producing Systems

---

## The Billionaire Mindset

The wealthy don't focus on:

**"How much can I spend?"**

They focus on:

**"How much can this produce?"**

Every dollar becomes an employee.

Every dollar gets assigned a job.

Every dollar is expected to generate a return.

---

## Why Most People Stay Stuck

Every time they make more money, they upgrade their lifestyle.

The wealthy upgrade their assets.

One group buys liabilities.

The other group buys cash flow.

---

## Think About This

If you received $10,000 today...

Would you buy something that loses value?

Or would you invest it into something that has the potential to produce income for years?

That single decision can change your financial future.

---

## The Goal

Don't spend your life working to buy liabilities.

Work to acquire assets that can help fund your lifestyle.

The wealthy don't become wealthy because they earn more.

They become wealthy because they consistently acquire assets.

One asset becomes two.

Two becomes five.

Five becomes ten.

That's how wealth compounds.

The rich focus on acquiring assets.

Everyone else focuses on acquiring liabilities.

A proper inventory count can show you:

Does the stock recorded in the system reflect reality?
Are there hidden losses, damage, or waste?
Are there slow-moving items?
Are purchases based on actual needs?
Is product cost calculated correctly?
Are inventory differences affecting profit margins?
And is internal control over stock actually effective?

The issue is not only having an inventory difference.

The bigger issue is that this difference can affect:

Cost of sales
Profit margin
Product pricing
Financial statements
Purchasing decisions
And cash flow

That is why a strong inventory count does not start on the counting day only.

It starts with a clear inventory system, proper documentation cycle, and accurate connection between purchases, sales, production, and waste.

At **FINXA**, we believe inventory is not just a number on the balance sheet.

Inventory is working capital tied inside the business, and any weakness in managing it can directly impact profitability and cash flow.

**Accurate inventory count means stronger control, clearer cost visibility, and smarter financial decisions.**

💸 Cuando una empresa empieza a tener problemas de flujo de efectivo, la reacción suele ser inmediata:

✔️ Retrasar pagos
✔️ Negociar con proveedores
✔️ Buscar financiamiento
✔️ Presionar la cobranza

Y aunque estas acciones pueden ayudar, rara vez atacan el verdadero origen del problema.

Porque el flujo de efectivo no nace en Tesorería. Nace mucho antes. Nace en las decisiones que la empresa toma todos los días.

📌 En las ventas que se realizan sin validar condiciones de cobro.

📌 En los inventarios que crecen más rápido que la demanda.

📌 En las compras que se autorizan sin una planeación clara.

📌 En proyectos que consumen recursos sin generar retorno.

📌 En gastos que parecen pequeños de forma individual, pero enormes cuando se acumulan.

Por eso, las empresas con mejor liquidez no son necesariamente las que más venden; son las que mejor convierten sus decisiones en efectivo.

⚠️ Vender no siempre significa cobrar.
⚠️ Facturar no siempre significa generar caja.
⚠️ Crecer no siempre significa fortalecer el negocio.

De hecho, algunas empresas han quebrado vendiendo más que nunca.

El flujo de efectivo es el reflejo de la disciplina operativa de toda la organización.

No es responsabilidad exclusiva de Finanzas. Es responsabilidad de todos.

Un liderazgo financiero sólido entiende que proteger la liquidez no consiste únicamente en administrar dinero.

Consiste en construir procesos, controles y decisiones que permitan que el dinero permanezca dentro del negocio.

Porque al final del día:

💡 La utilidad paga impuestos.
💡 El flujo de efectivo paga nóminas.

Y cuando la caja se agota, los estados financieros dejan de importar.

Une entreprise peut être rentable sur le papier et manquer de trésorerie. Clients qui paient en retard, stocks qui dorment, dette à rembourser. C’est tout l’objet de ce document : raisonner en cash qui rentre et qui sort réellement, pas en charges et produits comptables.

Le tableau se lit en trois flux. Le flux opérationnel, le cash généré par l’activité. Le flux d’investissement, l’argent dépensé en machines et acquisitions. Le flux de financement, l’argent levé ou rendu. La somme des trois donne la variation de trésorerie de l’année.

Au cœur du flux opérationnel se cache le BFR (besoin en fonds de roulement), et c’est là que beaucoup se trompent. Entre le moment où l’entreprise paie ses fournisseurs et celui où ses clients la paient, l’argent est immobilisé. Quand le BFR augmente, il consomme du cash. C’est le paradoxe de la croissance qui tue : une entreprise qui vend de plus en plus peut manquer de trésorerie en étant parfaitement rentable. À l’inverse, un supermarché encaisse comptant et paie ses fournisseurs à 60 jours : son cycle génère du cash.

Et tout se boucle : la trésorerie de fin d’année se retrouve à l’actif du bilan. Compte de résultat, bilan, flux de trésorerie : trois documents, un seul système.

Why is cash flow more important than income?

Many people believe that becoming rich is simply a matter of earning a high salary.

But income alone does not create financial freedom.

Cash flow does.

Cash flow is the money that continues to come in after all expenses have been paid.

This is the money that can be:

reinvested,

saved,

used to acquire more assets,

and eventually replace earned income.

A person can earn a very high salary and still struggle financially if expenses consume everything.

Another person may earn less but own assets that generate recurring cash flow every month.

Who is more financially secure?

The one whose assets continue producing income whether they work or not.

This is why many business owners and investors focus more on cash flow than on salary.

Cash flow creates options.

It gives you the ability to:

invest in new opportunities,

weather difficult periods,

reduce financial stress,

and build long-term wealth.

The ultimate goal is simple:

Build enough cash flow from assets to cover your living expenses.

At that point, work becomes a choice rather than a necessity.

Income can make you comfortable.

Cash flow can make you free.

One of the biggest cash flow killers for small businesses isn't bad sales. It's slow invoicing. 📄

Here are 5 ways to get paid faster - without awkward conversations:
1. Invoice immediately
The moment the job is done, or the goods delivered. Every day you wait is a day the client isn't paying.
2. Make your payment terms crystal clear
"Payment due upon receipt" and "net 30" mean very different things. Put the due date on the invoice, not just the terms.
3. Make it easy to pay
Bank transfer details on every invoice. Consider whether card payments or direct debit could work for your business.
4. Chase consistently - and early
A friendly reminder a couple of days before the due date is far less awkward than chasing a week after it.
5. Review your terms if late payment is a pattern

30-day terms are a habit, not a rule. Some businesses do very well on 14 days. A good bookkeeper will keep an eye on all of this for you, so nothing slips through the cracks.

Unpopular opinion: profit is one of the most misleading metrics in business.

I’ve seen “profitable” businesses constantly stressed about money… and genuinely strong businesses that don’t obsess over profit at all.

The biggest mistake business owners make is believing that profit equals financial health.

It doesn’t.

Profit is what your accountant calculates after the fact.
Cash flow is what determines whether you can actually survive the month.

And in real businesses, I see this pattern all the time:

-Profit on paper, but no cash in the bank
-VAT and tax bills creating panic when they land
-Growth that looks impressive but drains liquidity
-Owners delaying their own pay because “the numbers look fine”

Here’s the uncomfortable truth:

Most cash flow problems don’t come from bad businesses.

They come from growing businesses that aren’t financially controlled.

Growth eats cash. Fast.

So the question isn’t “are we profitable?”
It’s “can we survive our own success?”

The most resilient businesses I work with aren’t the most profitable on paper. They are the ones that understand timing, cash discipline, and financial control.

Would you rather look successful in your accounts… or actually feel in control of your business?

Why Profitable Businesses Still Face Cash Shortages

One of the biggest misconceptions in business is this:

"If the company is profitable, cash should never be a problem."

But many profitable businesses still face cash shortages.

Why?

Because profit and cash are not the same thing.

Profit is an accounting outcome.

Cash is operational reality.

A business may record strong sales and healthy profits on paper, yet still struggle to pay suppliers, salaries, or operational expenses on time.

The reason often lies in timing.

Customers may take 30, 60, or even 90 days to pay.

Inventory may need to be purchased immediately.

Vendors may require faster payments.

And operational costs continue regardless of when cash arrives.

This creates a gap.

The business is profitable —
but the money is not yet available when it is needed most.

Growth can make this challenge even bigger.

As sales increase, working capital requirements usually increase too.

More inventory.
Higher receivables.
Larger operational commitments.

Without proper cash-flow planning, growth itself can create liquidity pressure.

This is why experienced founders monitor more than revenue and profit.

They focus on cash-flow visibility.

They track collections carefully.
Plan for future obligations.
And ensure that business growth is supported by enough liquidity to sustain it comfortably.

Because profitability helps build value.

But cash flow keeps the business running.

And in the real world, businesses rarely struggle because they are unprofitable.

Many struggle because cash arrives later than pressure does.

Why Profitable Businesses Still Face Cash Shortages

One of the biggest misconceptions in business is this:

"If the company is profitable, cash should never be a problem."

But many profitable businesses still face cash shortages.

Why?

Because profit and cash are not the same thing.

Profit is an accounting outcome.

Cash is operational reality.

A business may record strong sales and healthy profits on paper, yet still struggle to pay suppliers, salaries, or operational expenses on time.

The reason often lies in timing.

Customers may take 30, 60, or even 90 days to pay.

Inventory may need to be purchased immediately.

Vendors may require faster payments.

And operational costs continue regardless of when cash arrives.

This creates a gap.

The business is profitable —
but the money is not yet available when it is needed most.

Growth can make this challenge even bigger.

As sales increase, working capital requirements usually increase too.

More inventory.
Higher receivables.
Larger operational commitments.

Without proper cash-flow planning, growth itself can create liquidity pressure.

This is why experienced founders monitor more than revenue and profit.

They focus on cash-flow visibility.

They track collections carefully.
Plan for future obligations.
And ensure that business growth is supported by enough liquidity to sustain it comfortably.

Because profitability helps build value.

But cash flow keeps the business running.

And in the real world, businesses rarely struggle because they are unprofitable.

Many struggle because cash arrives later than pressure does.

Your processor is holding $50K to $200K of your money right now. And you can probably get most of it back.

Rolling reserves are how high-risk processors protect themselves from chargebacks and refunds. The standard setup: 5-10% of your processing volume held for 180 days before being released back to you.

Sounds reasonable until you do the math.

A merchant processing $300K/month with a 10% rolling reserve has $180,000 of their own money sitting in a reserve account at any given time. That's working capital you could be using for inventory, ad spend, hiring, or runway.

What most merchants don't know: rolling reserves are negotiable.

After 6 months of clean processing (low chargebacks, no refund spikes, consistent volume), you have leverage to renegotiate:

→ Reduce the reserve percentage from 10% to 5%
→ Shorten the hold period from 180 days to 90
→ Convert a rolling reserve to a capped reserve (fixed dollar amount)
→ Eliminate the reserve entirely if your processing history is strong enough

Most merchants never ask. They assume the original terms are permanent. They're not.

If your reserve has been the same since day one and you've been processing cleanly for 6+ months, you have a case to make.

A liability takes money out of your pocket.

Liabilities can include: car payments, consumer debt, financed luxury items, and expenses that do not produce income.

This does not mean cars, houses, or luxury items are bad.

The real question is: Does this put money into my pocket, or take money out of my pocket?
Wealthy people usually buy assets first.
Then they use the cash flow from those assets to pay for liabilities.

Many people do the opposite: they buy liabilities first and hope to invest later.

That is why a good income alone does not guarantee lasting wealth.

The principle is simple: Acquire assets.
Increase cash flow.

Reinvest profits.

Repeat.

Over time, your assets begin to pay for your lifestyle.

Profitable on paper. Can't make payroll Friday.

This isn't a generic "cash flow problem." It's one of three very specific traps.

Trap 1: You spent money you hadn't earned yet. You billed the customer $80k early in the job. The cash came in. You used it for payroll, materials, paying down old bills. Now the job is finishing and the work still has to be delivered. You're finishing it on your own dime.

Trap 2: Your revenue isn't your cash. You completed $200k of work last quarter, and your P&L recognized all of it. But $30k is sitting in retainage. Another $40k is 60+ days out. You're profitable. $70k of that profit isn't in your account. CFMA's industry data confirms this pattern: ~40% of contractor assets sit in receivables, only 21% in cash.

Trap 3: You grew faster than your cash could carry. Three new jobs starting close together. Each needs materials and labor before the customer pays. Deposits don't cover the upfront. You're funding the start of every new job with operating cash from the last one. It works — until two jobs hit mobilization in the same week.

And there's a fourth that's worse than the first three: WIP isn't being run properly, so the P&L is showing profit on jobs that haven't actually earned it. The "profit" was never real to begin with.

The fix isn't a bigger line of credit or chasing customers harder. It's running WIP monthly so revenue on your P&L is real. Tracking retainage separately, not buried in AR. Building a 13-week cash forecast. Never bidding a job your cash can't carry.

A Modern Founder’s Guide to Sustainable Business Growth

In today's business environment, growth is easier to achieve than ever before.

But sustainable growth?

That is becoming much harder.

Many founders focus on scaling quickly.

More customers.
More revenue.
More expansion.

And while growth is important, speed alone does not create a stronger business.

Sustainable growth requires balance.

It requires growing without creating unnecessary pressure underneath the business.

Modern founders understand that growth starts with visibility.

They know their cash flow.
Understand their margins.
Track liquidity carefully.
And monitor financial health as closely as they monitor sales.

They also build systems before they become necessary.

Processes.
Reporting.
Team structures.
Operational controls.

Because growth eventually exposes every weakness in a business.

The stronger the foundation, the smoother the scaling journey.

Another important principle is alignment.

Funding should match business needs.
Expansion should match operational capacity.
And decision-making should support long-term stability, not just short-term momentum.

Sustainable founders also think differently about risk.

They don't avoid it.

They prepare for it.

They create financial buffers.
Plan for uncertainty.
And build businesses that can remain stable even when conditions change.

Because real success is not measured by how fast a company grows for one year.

It is measured by how consistently it can grow for many years.

The modern founder's goal is not just to build a bigger business.

It is to build a business that remains profitable, resilient, and in control while it grows.

And that is what sustainable growth truly looks like.

Za kvalitetno upravljanje poslovanjem potrebno je analizirati:
• nabavnu vrijednost prodane robe

• rabate van fakture

• ostale troškove povezane s proizvodom

Zato najprodavaniji proizvod nije nužno i najprofitabilniji proizvod.

Kontribucijski izvještaj po proizvodu omogućava menadžmentu da prepozna:
✅ koje proizvode treba dodatno razvijati

Uspješno upravljanje proizvodnim portfeljem ne temelji se samo na količini prodaje, već na razumijevanju stvarnog doprinosa svakog proizvoda rezultatu poslovanja.

🏠 TIPS FOR BUYING AN INVESTMENT PROPERTY

A great investment property isn't about how it looks on a Saturday tour — it's about how the numbers hold up over years. In a market like South Florida, where insurance, HOA fees, and seasonality all swing returns, the buyers who win are the ones who underwrite before they fall in love.

Here is what every investor should know 👇

1️⃣ RUN THE NUMBERS FIRST
Focus on cash flow, expenses, and return potential before emotion. Map out realistic rent, mortgage, taxes, insurance, and HOA, then see what's actually left. If the deal only works on best-case assumptions, it doesn't work.

2️⃣ STUDY LOCAL RENT DEMAND
Strong tenant demand is what keeps a property occupied and stable. Look at how fast comparable units lease, what they rent for, and who the renters are in that specific building or area — South Florida demand can vary block by block.

3️⃣ ESTIMATE REPAIRS HONESTLY
Budget realistically for updates, deferred maintenance, and the surprises that always show up. Better to over-estimate the rehab and be pleasantly surprised than get crushed by a roof, AC, or assessment you didn't plan for.

4️⃣ CHECK HOA & RENTAL RULES
Many condos and communities restrict leasing — minimum lease terms, rental caps, or waitlists that can derail a rental plan. Read the docs and confirm the rules fit your strategy before you close, not after.

5️⃣ BUY FOR RETURNS, NOT HYPE
A great-looking property still has to make financial sense. Beautiful finishes don't pay your mortgage — net returns do. Let the math, not the marketing, decide whether it's a buy.

Most MSME businesses don't fail because of bad products or poor service. They fail because of financial mistakes that were completely avoidable. Here are the 5 most common ones 👇

After working with hundreds of small businesses, the same financial mistakes appear again and again.

The good news? All of them are preventable — once you know what to watch for.

❌ Mistake 1: Mixing personal and business finances
Using one bank account for both personal expenses and business transactions is one of the most damaging habits an MSME owner can have.

It makes your financial picture unclear, your taxes complicated, and your credibility weak in front of any formal financial partner.
✅ Fix: Open a dedicated business current account. Use it exclusively for business income and expenses.

❌ Mistake 2: No cash flow forecast
Most MSME owners manage cash reactively — they check their balance when they need to pay something.
✅ Fix: Prepare a simple 8-week cash flow forecast every month. Map expected inflows and outflows.

❌ Mistake 3: Ignoring receivables until it's urgent
Unpaid invoices are money you've already earned but haven't received. Letting them age beyond 45–60 days is a silent cash flow drain.
✅ Fix: Follow up on every invoice at 15, 30, and 45 days. Make it a system, not a reaction.

❌ Mistake 4: No financial records for the first 1–2 years
"I'll start maintaining proper books once the business grows." By then, you have 2 years of invisible financial history that no formal partner can verify.
✅ Fix: Start proper bookkeeping from Day 1 — even if it's a simple spreadsheet maintained by your CA.

❌ Mistake 5: Taking on more financial obligation than cash flow supports
The cost of any financial commitment — rent, supplier agreements, equipment — must be measured against your actual monthly cash flow, not projected future revenue.
✅ Fix: The simple rule — total fixed monthly obligations should not exceed 50% of your average monthly cash inflow.

⁠
Why?⁠
⁠
Because cash and profit are not the same thing.⁠
⁠
We regularly see businesses caught out by:⁠
• VAT liabilities⁠
• corporation tax payments⁠
• slow-paying customers⁠
• increasing wage costs⁠
• stock purchasing commitments⁠
• director drawings⁠
• seasonal fluctuations⁠
⁠
A business can appear highly profitable while simultaneously struggling with day-to-day cash availability.⁠
⁠
This is why forecasting and regular financial reviews are becoming increasingly important, particularly in a higher cost environment where margins are under pressure.⁠
⁠
The businesses coping best right now are typically not the ones obsessing over turnover alone.⁠
⁠
They are the ones:⁠
• monitoring cash flow regularly⁠
• understanding their numbers in detail⁠
• planning ahead for liabilities⁠
• reviewing profitability by client, product or service⁠
• making informed decisions early⁠
⁠
Good financial management is no longer simply about year-end compliance.⁠
⁠
It is increasingly about visibility, planning and being able to make confident decisions before problems arise.⁠
⁠
In the current climate, strong cash flow management is often what separates resilient businesses from vulnerable ones.⁠

One thing I’ve learned working in A/R is that a promise to pay isn’t something I cross off my list.

It’s something I track.

When a customer gives me a payment date, I document it and make sure there’s a follow-up plan behind it. I’ve seen too many situations where everyone assumes the payment is coming, only to find out later that nothing was actually moving forward.

What I’ve found is that the first broken promise is usually worth investigating.

Instead of immediately asking for another payment date, I try to understand what changed.

Was there an approval delay? Is there a dispute nobody mentioned before? Has cash become tight? Did the invoice simply get pushed down the priority list?

The reason matters because it tells you what action to take next.

And if the same account keeps making promises that aren’t being kept, I stop focusing on the promises and start focusing on the root cause. That often means involving additional contacts, escalating internally, or having a more direct conversation about what’s preventing payment.

In my experience, repeated broken promises are usually a symptom of a bigger issue.

The goal isn’t to collect promises to pay.

The goal is to understand what’s standing between the invoice and the cash.

Kenapa perkara ini berlaku?

Salah satu puncanya ialah "lifestyle inflation" iaitu apabila gaya hidup dan perbelanjaan turut meningkat setiap kali pendapatan bertambah. Akhirnya, simpanan masih tidak bertambah walaupun gaji semakin besar.

Berikut 5 tanda anda mungkin sedang hidup melebihi kemampuan:

1️⃣ Perbelanjaan kecil yang tidak dipantau semakin banyak setiap bulan.

2️⃣ Gaji habis sebelum hujung bulan tiba.

3️⃣ Terlalu bergantung kepada kad kredit atau kemudahan Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL).

4️⃣ Simpanan kecemasan tidak mencukupi atau langsung tiada.

5️⃣ Pendapatan meningkat tetapi keadaan kewangan masih tidak berubah.

Hidup melebihi kemampuan tidak semestinya bermaksud berbelanja mewah. Kadangkala ia berlaku secara perlahan melalui tabiat kewangan harian yang nampak biasa tetapi memberi kesan besar dalam jangka panjang.

Semakin awal anda mengenal pasti tanda-tanda ini, semakin mudah untuk memperbaiki kedudukan kewangan, mengurangkan tekanan dan membina masa depan yang lebih stabil.

Tatsächlich können sich die Steuerlast und die individuelle Einnahmesituation durch die Spekulationsfrist erheblich ändern. Nach drei Jahren Haltezeit entfällt die Spekulationssteuer, was bei der Finanzierungslogik entscheidend ist.

Wesentlich sind daher die Überlegungen zur Strategie der Haltedauer. Profis analysieren die potenziellen Einnahmen nicht nur isoliert, sondern im Kontext der Steuerfolgen. Informationen zu Finanzierungskosten, möglichen Wertsteigerungen und voraussichtlichen Verkaufszeitpunkten sind dabei unerlässlich.

Ein typischer Denkfehler besteht darin, Einnahmequellen zu optimistisch einzuschätzen, ohne die steuerlichen Abzüge realistisch zu betrachten. Dies kann zu einer falschen Einschätzung der Rentabilität führen und möglicherweise bedeutende finanzielle Verluste mit sich bringen.

Personal vs Business.
Which account keeps your Ltd legal, and pays you faster?

If you're a UK limited company running through a personal bank account, every one of these six dimensions is quietly
working against you.

01 — Liability.
A limited company is its own legal entity. The whole point is that company debts are not your personal debts. Mixing company money through your personal account is the clearest way to "pierce the corporate veil" and end up
personally liable for things you incorporated to be protected from.

02 — Tax.
HMRC requires "a clear division between the company's finances and those of the owners and directors." Personal accounts blur that line. Mixed records make Corporation Tax returns harder, expense claims weaker, and HMRC investigations more likely.

03 — Speed.
Untangling shared transactions at year-end is the bit accountants charge most for. A clean business account means statements flow straight into Xero or FreeAgent.
A personal account is a download, a tag, and an explanation per line.

04 — Credibility.
Some accounts cap inbound business payments. No caps, no surprise holds when a £4k invoice lands.

Built for the volume. Same-day Faster Payments. No arbitrary holiday spend cap of company money.

06 — Trust.
Sort code routes to a business name that matches your CRM. Procurement reviewer's favourite reason to send it
back: the sort code clears it on the first pass.

Nelle aziende strutturate, l’ufficio amministrativo interno è spesso assorbito dalle scadenze quotidiane: fatturazione, registrazioni, adempimenti. C’è però una sottile linea di demarcazione tra un’azienda che “registra il passato” e una che “pianifica il futuro”: la gestione predittiva della tesoreria.
Per una media impresa, ottimizzare i flussi di cassa non significa semplicemente verificare il saldo bancario a fine mese, ma trasformare i dati finanziari in decisioni strategiche.
Perché la tesoreria è il vero motore della crescita?

1️⃣ Sostiene gli investimenti senza tensioni: permette di capire se l’autofinanziamento è sufficiente per supportare nuovi progetti (macchinari, R&S, assunzioni) o se è necessario calibrare il mix delle fonti di finanziamento esterne.
2️⃣ Ottimizza il Working Capital: monitorare i tempi medi di incasso e di pagamento consente di liberare la liquidità intrappolata nel capitale circolante netto.
3️⃣ Migliora il rating bancario: presentarsi agli istituti di credito con un budget di tesoreria affidabile e scenari di stress test strutturati aumenta il potere contrattuale dell’azienda e riduce il costo del denaro.
Il ruolo del vostro reparto amministrativo (e il nostro): la vostra struttura interna possiede già i dati grezzi. Il passo successivo è strutturarli in modelli di Cash Flow Forecasting (a 3, 6 o 12 mesi) per anticipare i colli di bottiglia finanziari prima che si verifichino.

🚨 How Much Revenue Does Your Business Need Every Month Just to Stay Open?

Many business owners know how much revenue they generated last month, but very few know their break-even number.

Your break-even point is the amount of revenue your business must generate to cover expenses before producing a profit.

At break-even:

✅ Revenue equals expenses
✅ Bills are paid
✅ Costs are covered
✅ There is no profit and no loss

Every dollar earned above your break-even point contributes to profit.

To understand your break-even point, you need to understand three key accounting concepts:

📌 Fixed Costs – Expenses that generally remain the same each month, such as rent, insurance, software subscriptions, loan payments, and administrative expenses.

📌 Variable Costs – Expenses that increase as sales increase, such as materials, subcontractors, direct labor, merchant fees, and supplies.

📌 Gross Profit – The amount remaining after direct costs are deducted from revenue. Gross profit helps cover overhead expenses and generate net profit.

Understanding these numbers can help answer important business questions:

• Are we charging enough?
• Can we afford to hire?
• Can we purchase new equipment?
• How much revenue do we need each month to remain profitable?

One of the most common mistakes we see is business owners relying solely on their bank balance to measure success.

Your bank balance tells you how much cash is available today.

Your financial statements tell you whether your business is actually profitable.

Knowing your numbers helps you make informed decisions, manage risk, and build a stronger business.

Then they discover cost segregation.

Cost segregation is a tax strategy that analyzes a property and identifies components that may qualify for shorter depreciation schedules than the building itself.

Instead of treating the entire property as one asset, a cost segregation study separates qualifying items such as flooring, appliances, lighting, landscaping, parking areas, and certain site improvements.

Why does that matter?

Because different components may be depreciated over different time periods.

That can accelerate depreciation deductions, which may improve cash flow and reduce taxable income in the earlier years of ownership.

The property doesn't change.

The way the property is analyzed changes.

Demain dans le Portail, on parle et surtout on vit « Cocréation ».

Un sujet exaltant que je triture depuis une vingtaine d’années.

Étudiante en sciences sociales, j’étais passionnée par tout ce qui relevait de l’action collective : qu’est ce qui fait individuellement et collectivement que l’on va dans le mur ou qu’au contraire la dynamique prend un tour inattendu pour aller vers une solution créative et bénéfique ?

Consultante, j’ai animé pendant 10 ans des réunions, des groupes de travail, des séminaires, avec cette même question en tête. Et dans l’ensemble, je ressortais frustrée de mes interventions : j’avais la sensation de rester à un niveau de travail superficiel. De ne pas craquer le code de la Cocréation.

La Cocréation doit pour moi amener à quelque chose de véritablement Nouveau et qui est plus grand que la somme des parties. 
Et à mon sens, pour en arriver là, il y a un travail colossal à mener.

Un travail déjà individuel : comment cocréer si je ne suis pas connecté à ma Source de Création ? Comment cocréer si je n’ai pas conscience de mon Univers Créatif, dans ses aspects métaphysiques et physiques ?

Et un travail collectif, ensuite. Ce travail touche à des questions fascinantes : y-a-t-il des convergences métaphysiques suffisamment proches pour que la Cocréation soit fluide ? Y-a-t-il des complémentarités suffisamment présentes pour expandre le champ des possibles et faire croître l’ensemble des protagonistes à travers l’acte créatif ? Y-a-t-il un désir véritable de cocréer ? Y-a-t-il un cadre qui permette à la Cocréation de se déployer ?

Loin d’être une action mécanique, un assemblage de parties prenantes ou une technique, la Cocréation est pour moi un Art.
Un Art qui requiert une maîtrise de sa Conscience autant qu’une précision chirurgicale.

(Œuvre : Carte d’Oracle « La Cocréation », peinture devant laquelle un ami ingénieur s’est exclamé : « On dirait de l’intrication quantique ». Une chose que j’adore avec mes amis, c’est qu’ils comprennent tout ce que je fais sans que j’ai besoin de le leur expliquer 😆.)

Tecnologie dirompenti, piattaforme digitali e intelligenza artificiale: perché anche le grandi aziende possono perdere il futuro

La storia dell’innovazione tecnologica è piena di paradossi. Molte aziende leader, pur essendo solide, ben gestite e ricche di risorse, non riescono a mantenere la propria posizione quando cambiano le tecnologie, i mercati o i comportamenti dei consumatori. Non falliscono necessariamente perché sono incompetenti o distratte. Spesso accade il contrario: falliscono proprio perché applicano con coerenza le regole del buon management tradizionale. Ascoltano i clienti più importanti, investono nei prodotti più redditizi, migliorano ciò che già funziona e concentrano le risorse dove i margini sono più alti.

L’articolo scientifico di Vincent English, Disruptive Technologies and the Incumbent’s Dilemma in Navigating the Digital and AI Era, riprende la teoria dell’innovazione dirompente formulata da Bower e Christensen e la aggiorna alla luce dell’economia digitale, delle piattaforme e dell’intelligenza artificiale generativa. Il punto centrale è che la “disruption” non è semplicemente una tecnologia nuova o più potente. È un cambiamento che ridefinisce il valore: ciò che all’inizio sembra inferiore, marginale o poco interessante può migliorare rapidamente, conquistare nuovi utenti e infine mettere in crisi gli attori dominanti.

Oggi questo processo è ancora più rapido e complesso. Netflix, Uber, Airbnb, NVIDIA e OpenAI mostrano che la competizione non avviene più soltanto tra prodotti, ma tra ecosistemi, dati, reti di utenti, infrastrutture tecnologiche e modelli di business. Capire l’innovazione dirompente significa quindi comprendere perché il futuro spesso nasce ai margini del mercato, in spazi che le aziende dominanti tendono a sottovalutare.

The Real Meaning of Disruption

Most people get disruption wrong. They think disruption is about breakthrough technology.

It isn’t.

According to Clayton Christensen, disruptive innovations rarely start as better products. They start as simpler, cheaper and more accessible solutions that incumbents dismiss.

Market leaders focus on their best customers. They keep improving performance.

But eventually they deliver more than many customers actually need.

That’s when disruption happens.

New entrants serve overlooked customers or non-consumers. Their products may initially seem inferior. Yet they improve, gain traction and eventually challenge the leaders.

The personal computer wasn’t more powerful than the mainframe.

Netflix wasn’t better than Blockbuster on day one.

The real power of disruption is not superior technology.

It is making products and services accessible to more people.

For innovators, this raises an important question:

Are you making your products better?

Or are you making them accessible to people who cannot use them today?

That is where disruption often begins.

Most people think our biggest problems are inflation, debt, corruption, poverty, housing, healthcare, climate change, political division, or economic instability.

They're wrong.

Those are symptoms.

The real problem is that humanity is operating on disconnected systems.

Our financial systems don't communicate efficiently.
Our governments don't coordinate effectively.
Our institutions optimize for separate goals.
Our currencies compete instead of connecting.
Our data exists in silos.

1. "Pseudo Harmony" (Budaya Asal Bos Senang)
Definisi: Ketenangan semu organisasi yang dibangun di atas pembungkaman pendapat, ego sektoral, dan ketakutan staf menyuarakan kebenaran.
Indikator: Kritik dianggap tidak loyal, muncul "raja kecil" di unit kerja, dan laporan performa selalu disajikan manis tanpa dinamika.
Dampak: Hilangnya mekanisme koreksi mandiri, stagnasi inovasi total, serta rapat hanya menjadi formalitas tanpa solusi.
Konklusi: Organisasi hancur saat kompetensi dikalahkan oleh ego struktural dan inovasi dianggap sebagai ancaman politis.

2. Dampak Pemangku Kepentingan
Pasien: Bingung karena info antar-unit bertolak belakang; lelah menghadapi petugas kaku dan masalah lama yang terus dibiarkan.
Staf: Memilih masa bodoh demi menggugurkan kewajiban karena tahu siapa yang bicara lebih penting daripada bobot ide.
Manajerial: Terjebak delusi rapat yang tenang, menerima laporan bagus di atas kertas namun bingung operasional lapangan stagnan.

3. Solusi Strategis: "Reliability Culture" (Prinsip HRO)
Prinsip: Budaya keandalan dibentuk bukan untuk memaksa kepatuhan buta, melainkan membangun sistem yang bersih, jelas, dan sesuai realita.
Karakteristik: Meritokrasi berbasis kepakaran, diskusi faktual, serta menjadikan staf lini depan sebagai radar dinamika operasional.
Fokus: Dobrak praktik kolegisme dan patronase birokrasi, lalu ganti dengan ekosistem pembelajaran High Reliability Organization (HRO).

Kesimpulan Implikatif: Ubah paradigma kepemimpinan dari "siapa yang bicara" menjadi "apa bobot pernyataannya." Memelihara harmoni palsu hanya akan melumpuhkan deteksi kerusakan sistemik. Tumbuhkan Reliability Culture agar kebijakan manajemen menjadi realistis dan relevan dengan lapangan.

Fujifilm und Kodak. 2000. Nahezu identische Ausgangslage. Beide Weltmarktführer in analogen Filmen. Beide mit rund 13 Mrd. USD Umsatz. Zwölf Jahre später meldet einer Insolvenz an.

Der Wendepunkt kam nicht durch bessere Produkte.
Nicht durch eine Markenoffensive.
Und nicht durch externes Kapital.
Was entschied: eine Frage, die Kodak nie gestellt hat.

CEO Shigetaka Komori machte 2000 keine Panikentscheidung.
Er machte eine Inventur.

Nicht: In welchen neuen Markt gehen wir?
Sondern: Was wissen wir, das niemand anderes hat?

Antwort: 45.000 Materialtechnologien aus 60 Jahren Filmforschung.

Kollagen, der Hauptbestandteil von Fotoemulsionen, ist chemisch identisch mit dem Wirkstoff in Antiaging-Kosmetik. Das wurde zu Astalift.
TAC-Folie, ursprünglich Schutzschicht für Fotofilme, ist der kritische Bestandteil in LCD-Display-Polarisatoren. Marktanteil heute: über 70 %.
Chemische Verbindungen aus der Filmentwicklung wurden direkt in pharmazeutische Bildgebung und Diagnostik übertragen.

Das ist der Punkt, den viele übersehen:

Diversifikation ohne Inventur ist Kapitalvernichtung.
Fujifilm hat keine neuen Märkte gesucht.
Es hat den eigenen technologischen Kern in neue Märkte übersetzt.

Fujifilm verschob sich von:

Fotochemie zu pharmazeutischer Wirkstoffforschung
Filmschutztechnologie zu LCD-Infrastruktur
Produktverteidigung zu Plattformstrategie
Reaktion auf Marktdruck zu struktureller Destillation

Und genau hier scheitern die meisten Unternehmen in der Krise:

Sie fragen, welche neuen Märkte sie betreten sollen.
Sie fragen nicht, welchen Kern sie bereits besitzen.

Kodak hatte dieselbe Technologiebasis wie Fujifilm.
Es fehlte nicht die Ressource. Es fehlte die Frage.

In Dallas erschien die Zukunft nicht als Bedrohung, sondern als unbequeme Position in einer Gewinnrechnung.

Blockbusters Verzicht auf den Kauf von Netflix zeigt, wie Rentabilitätskennzahlen zur institutionellen Verteidigung gegen strategische Erneuerung werden können.

Im September 2000 trat Netflix in Dallas nicht als globaler Streamingkonzern auf, sondern als verlustträchtige Internetfirma nach dem Platzen der Dotcom-Euphorie. Das Angebot war nüchtern: Blockbuster sollte Netflix für 50 Mio. USD kaufen; Reed Hastings, Marc Randolph und Barry McCarthy wollten das Onlinegeschäft aufbauen. Die Episode wird oft als arroganter Irrtum erzählt. Diese Lesart ist eingängig, aber zu flach.

Der eigentliche Konflikt lag weniger in einem fehlenden Blick für das Internet als in einer Erfolgslogik, die den bestehenden Gewinn schützte. Blockbuster meldete 2004 rund 9.100 Filialen und 6,1 Mrd. USD Umsatz. Gleichzeitig waren verspätete Rückgaben ein relevanter Ergebnisbaustein: Blockbuster hatte für 2005 den direkten Effekt entfallender Säumnisgebühren auf 400 bis 450 Mio. USD Umsatz und 250 bis 300 Mio. USD operatives Ergebnis geschätzt.

Damit wurde Netflix nicht nur als kleines, defizitäres Unternehmen bewertet. Es bedrohte eine interne Architektur aus Filialnetzen, Mietverträgen, Personal, Inventar, operativen Kennzahlen und Kundengewohnheiten. Jede digitale Beschleunigung hätte zunächst Kennzahlen belastet, an denen Blockbusters Stärke gemessen wurde.

Das ist die institutionelle Falle reifer Unternehmen. Sie erkennen Disruption oft früher, als spätere Legenden behaupten. Doch wenn Kapitalmarkt, Management und operative Organisation auf den Schutz des aktuellen Margenprofils kalibriert sind, erscheint eine Zukunftsinvestition wie Selbstbeschädigung.

In 1999, Marc Benioff walked into the enterprise software world and effectively declared war on a multi-billion-dollar industry standard.
At the time, conventional wisdom was absolute: software had to be expensive, required months of tedious installation, and lived strictly behind a company’s firewall.
Benioff’s radical proposition? CRM should be delivered entirely as Software as a Service (SaaS).
The incumbents laughed. Analysts dismissed it. Investors hesitated.
But that is the burden of the forerunner. When you are the first to cross into uncharted territory, you don't find a paved road, you find intense resistance.
The Blueprint for Disruptive Leadership
What separates iconic leaders from the rest isn't just a good idea; it's the stamina to defend it. Innovation and grit are two sides of the same coin. To scale a radical concept, you must be willing to endure the discomfort of being misunderstood and/or disliked for a very long time.
You can present data and you can build a flawless business case. But without the raw courage to propose an uncomfortable idea and the grit to see it through, your vision will die in a conference room.
The DNA of an Industry Pathfinder
Being an industry pathfinder requires a rare mix of courage, grit, and absolute conviction. Pathfinders don’t wait for permission or validation from the market. They challenge the status quo because they possess the foresight to see a better way long before anyone else can even imagine it.
By standing firm against the critics, Benioff didn't just build Salesforce, he cleared the path for an entire generation of businesses. That single, defiant proposition birthed the trillion-dollar cloud revolution.

The universe isn't empty space with a few galaxies floating around. It has a skeleton.

NASA's James Webb Space Telescope just gave us the clearest look at it ever — a map of the Cosmic Web: the vast network of dark matter filaments and gas that connects every galaxy in existence.

The numbers are hard to process: 164,000 galaxies. 13.7 billion years of history. One image.

The team behind it — led by PhD student Hossein Hatamnia and Professor Bahram Mobasher at UC Riverside — used COSMOS-Web, the largest survey ever conducted by JWST, covering a patch of sky three times the size of a full Moon. 

Their infrared instruments detected galaxies invisible to any previous telescope, tracing the web all the way back to when the universe was just one billion years old.

And here's what makes this genuinely mind-bending: this structure has always been there. We've been living inside it for 13.7 billion years. We just didn't have the tools to see it.
Until now.

Quand j’ai commencé ma carrière dans le conseil, je m’étais dit que le Franglais ne passerait pas par moi.

Et puis, au bout de quelques années, j’ai abdiqué. 
Je suis devenue un Maître en Franglais. 
Le point confortable ? Je faisais partie intégrante de la tribu.
Le prix à payer ? Je me suis éloignée encore plus de mon véritable langage.

Retrouver les mots qui peuplent mon Monde fait partie du chemin que j’ai parcouru ces dernières années.
Un chemin qui a supposé - et je pèse mes mots - de me désintoxiquer. Tout mon Être était pollué de termes et de tournures de phrases qui n’avaient absolument rien à voir avec moi. Et qui me donnaient, si j’y étais véritablement attentive, une sensation de sang dans le bouche et de contraction dans les tripes, assortie d’une vague envie de mourir.

Au cours de ce processus de désintoxication, le Franglais est bien évidemment parti. 
En m’en séparant je me suis rendue compte de deux choses : il me donnait la sensation d’être cool, de faire partie de cet univers mondialisé à la pointe de la modernité. Formulé autrement : il me narcissisait. Et il me permettait de vivre en mode robot, au lieu de plonger dans mes profondeurs et de les ramener à la surface pour enfin m’exprimer telle que j’étais.

J’ai dû accepter ce qui me semblait inacceptable : mon style romanesque, conceptuel, ésotérique, poétique. Ce style à 1 000 lieues de la communication business et qui soulevait chez mon Humain Normé Terrifié des montagnes de peur et de honte. 

Mais, en acceptant cet inacceptable a priori, j’ai retrouvé ce qui est porteur d’une valeur infinie : j’ai retrouvé la puissance de mon Verbe Créateur. J’ai retrouvé la Vie.

THE WARNING ⚠️
→ In 1995, Agfa’s own engineers projected digital would crush film by 2005. The board read the report and filed it away.

THE DOUBLE-DOWN 🏗️

THE COLLAPSE 💥
→ On May 27, 2005, AgfaPhoto filed for insolvency with €2.5B in debt. 1,800 workers lost their jobs in a weekend. The brand survives only as a logo licensed to others.

THE LESSON 🧠
→ Fujifilm saw the same data and pivoted into cosmetics, medical imaging and materials. Same threat. Different choice. One company exists. The other is a museum.

The real risk isn’t missing the future. It’s seeing it clearly and choosing to protect the past anyway.

The USTR is also considering a mechanism that would allow limited quantities of textile and apparel imports to enter the United States at reduced tariff rates. The establishment of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) marks a pivotal shift in Southeast Asian economic integration. By pairing Johor’s land availability and manufacturing capacity with Singapore’s global financial muscle, the zone has created a high-velocity business corridor. However, as thousands of companies, data centers, and advanced manufacturing plants expand across this border, they face an unexpected roadblock: the frictional cost of moving capital.

While physical cross-border travel is being streamlined through passport-free QR immigration trials, the financial rails behind them remain bogged down by legacy legacy architectures. To unlock the full potential of the JS-SEZ, the region needs a parallel leap forward in payment infrastructure: on-chain cross-border stablecoin settlement.

Why Stablecoins Fit the Special Economic Zone? 

Stablecoins, cryptographic tokens pegged 1:1 to fiat currencies like USD, SGD, or MYR, offer a  programmable, internet-native alternative to traditional banking rails. Within an economic zone like the JS-SEZ, they serve as a digital ledger that bridges two distinct regulatory jurisdictions.

Instead of waiting for multiple clearinghouses to reconcile ledgers, stablecoins utilize public or permissioned blockchains to achieve atomic settlement. Money moves from a Singaporean parent company’s wallet to a Johor subsidiary’s wallet in under three seconds, operating 24/7/365. This accelerates supply chain velocity, allowing cargo clearance and supplier payments to happen simultaneously.

By passing directly from sender to receiver, stablecoins eliminate the chain of correspondent banks. For manufacturing components moving between Singapore and Johor, a company can settle a multi-million dollar invoice for fractions of a cent in network gas fees, drastically reducing operational overhead.

Using smart contracts, payments within the SEZ can be tied directly to physical milestones. For instance, a stablecoin payment can be locked in a digital escrow and automatically released to a Malaysian logistics provider the exact moment a digitised cargo clearance sensor registers that the delivery truck has crossed the Second Link

The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone represents the future of ASEAN’s industrial and digital economy. However, a 21st-century economic zone cannot run efficiently on 20th-century financial rails.

By legalizing and structuring regulated stablecoin settlement flows through compliance hubs like Labuan, Malaysia can offer international investors an unmatched operational ecosystem. The first movers to bridge the physical connectivity of the economic zone with the digital speed of programmable asset settlement will ultimately set the standard for cross-border commerce across the region.

Kenapa tiba-tiba semua orang jualan seblak, cilok, gorengan, dan cimol? 
Jawabannya bukan karena mereka jadi wirausahawan. 
Jawabannya karena mereka tidak punya pilihan lain.

Pertama tentang konsep yang paling penting untuk dipahami:

Dalam ilmu ekonomi tenaga kerja ada dua jenis wirausaha yang sangat berbeda.

Opportunity entrepreneurship berwirausaha karena melihat peluang pasar, ada inovasi, ada riset, ada rencana bisnis yang matang.

Necessity entrepreneurship berwirausaha karena terpaksa. Karena tidak ada pilihan lain. 
Karena kalau tidak jualan tidak bisa makan hari ini.

Dan mayoritas besar dari ledakan pedagang kaki lima kuliner yang kita lihat sekarang masuk ke kategori kedua. 
Bukan wirausahawan. 

Mereka adalah pengangguran yang menyamarkan statusnya dengan gerobak tepung.

Dan ini kenapa tepung dan aci yang dipilih
bukan karena cinta kuliner:

Modal paling rendah. 
Tidak butuh keahlian khusus. 
Tidak perlu izin. 
Tidak perlu riset pasar. 
Tidak ada resep rahasia yang perlu dijaga.

Beberapa kilogram tepung, minyak goreng curah, penyedap sintetis, bubuk cabai, dan wajan aluminium dan seseorang sudah bisa mengklaim punya usaha.

Bagi yang baru dapat surat PHK dari pabrik garmen ini adalah jaring pengaman terakhir. 
Bagi ratusan ribu sarjana yang lamarannya tidak pernah dijawab  ini bukan tentang membangun warisan bisnis. Ini tentang memastikan ada beras yang bisa dimasak besok pagi.

Dan ini tentang angka pengangguran yang paling sering disalahartikan:
BPS melaporkan pengangguran terbuka Februari 2026 di angka 7,24 juta orang atau 4,68%. 
Pemerintah menyebutnya sebagai keberhasilan.

Tapi angka itu menipu. 
Karena seseorang yang berjualan gorengan tiga jam sehari secara resmi tercatat sebagai bekerja bukan pengangguran.

Dalam ilmu ekonomi ini disebut pengangguran terselubung secara administratif bekerja, tapi produktivitas ekonomi marginalnya sangat rendah, tidak sesuai kapasitas atau keahliannya.

Dan buktinya sangat jelas: proporsi pekerja di sektor informal Indonesia secara persisten berada di 57 sampai 60% dari total angkatan kerja. 

Lebih dari separuh orang yang dihitung sebagai "bekerja" sebenarnya berada di sektor yang tidak ada jaminan kesehatan, tidak ada asuransi, tidak ada dana pensiun.

Dan ini tentang kanibalisme ekonomi yang paling menyedihkan:

Ketika satu pedagang cimol terlihat ramai minggu depan muncul 10 gerobak cimol dalam radius 100 meter. Semua menjual produk identik. 
Menyasar konsumen yang sama. 
Dengan harga yang sama.

Mereka tidak sedang bersaing dengan korporasi multinasional. 
Mereka sedang bersaing dengan sesama yang baru saja kena PHK dari pabrik yang sama.

Dan kue yang diperebutkan tidak membesar justru menyusut. Karena daya beli masyarakat sedang hancur. Kelas menengah turun kasta. 
Inflasi menggerus pendapatan. 
Pinjol mencekik. 
Uang yang beredar untuk beli jajan pinggir jalan makin sedikit.

Hasilnya: perang harga yang brutal. 
Margin yang sudah setipis kertas makin menipis. 
Dan tidak ada yang menang.

Dan ini tentang ironi terbesar yang jarang dibicarakan:
Indonesia adalah negara yang jutaan penduduknya menggantungkan hidup pada tepung terigu tapi tidak bisa menanam gandum satu biji pun di tanahnya sendiri.

Hampir 100% kebutuhan gandum Indonesia diimpor dari Australia, Kanada, Amerika, Rusia, Ukraina. 
Dan volume impor itu diperkirakan terus naik rata-rata 6,38% per tahun hingga bisa menembus 21,67 juta ton.

Artinya: ketika ada El Nino di Australia, ketika ada perang di Ukraina, ketika rupiah melemah terhadap dolar harga tepung di pasar tradisional langsung naik. 

Dan yang pertama kena dampaknya adalah pedagang gorengan yang tidak punya instrumen lindung nilai, tidak bisa menaikkan harga, dan tidak bisa memangkas margin yang sudah nol.

The global logistics landscape is undergoing a structural shift where land-based supply chains are rapidly matching and in some corridors, outpacing maritime transport in pure operational velocity. At the vanguard of this transformation is the Bukit Kayu Hitam Special Border Economic Zone (SBEZ). Covering approximately 11,000 acres of strategically positioned land at the border of Kedah, Malaysia, and Sadao, Thailand, the SBEZ functions as the definitive "Zero Mile Zone" for the Northern Corridor Economic Region (NCER).

Yet, while multi-national freight forwarders and anchor logistics giants process millions of tons of cargo through this corridor, the underlying financial settlement layers remain analog, fragmented, and exposed to severe currency friction. To maximize the SBEZ’s structural "first load advantage," the integration of on-chain, compliant stablecoin payment rails offers an immediate path to accelerating capital velocity between Malaysia and Thailand.

The Bukit Kayu Hitam border is the primary gateway for over RM40 billion to RM70 billion in annual cross-border overland trade. Raw materials enter from Thailand to be processed into high-value-added exports via KSTP, while industrial components move fluidly north.  However, the banking infrastructure supporting this 11,000-acre corridor is heavily bottlenecked: 

Land transport relies on extreme real-time efficiency. When a Thai logistics provider handles Less-than-Truckload (LTL) shipments or cross-docking at the BKH ICD, delays in clearing international bank transfers stall operations. Legacy correspondent banking models cannot settle capital at the pace trucks move across the border. Businesses in the SBEZ must juggle Malaysian Ringgit (MYR), Thai Baht (THB), and US Dollars (USD) for international invoicing. Each swap incurs substantial foreign exchange spreads, compounding overhead costs for manufacturers operating on tight margins inside the managed industrial parks. Traditional trade finance instruments, like Letters of Credit (LCs), require tedious manual documentation checks across domestic jurisdictions, keeping working capital locked up for days while goods are already sitting in Free Commercial Zone warehouses. 

By embedding fiat-pegged stablecoins (such as regulated USD, SGD, or local-currency tokenized deposits) directly into the SBEZ’s digital infrastructure, the corridor can achieve atomic, real-time settlement. Through open, regulated stablecoin networks, a manufacturing plant in the Kedah Science & Technology Park can instantly settle invoices with a parts supplier in Thailand. Payments clear and reconcile natively on-chain 24/7/365, allowing logistics operators to immediately authorize truck dispatchment post-customs clearance without waiting for next-day bank verification.

The BKH ICD features 24/7 dedicated customs lanes and extensive container repair and reefer yard facilities. Using smart contracts on an enterprise blockchain layer, payment handling can be programmatically tied to data from the Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) database.

The implementation of stablecoins in the Bukit Kayu Hitam SBEZ aligns perfectly with Malaysia’s broader goals for regional development, national industrialization, and shared economic prosperity. By removing cross-border transaction latency, the SBEZ provides an unparalleled environment for Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). International manufacturers can construct green-certified, smart production facilities within the NCT InnoSphere or KSTP knowing that their supply-chain settlement infrastructure matches the bleeding-edge velocity of their automated assembly lines.

Furthermore, because stablecoin payment rails allow seamless integration with wholesale digital currency platforms and tokenized corporate deposit engines, the SBEZ can interface natively with Tier-1 commercial banking corridors across ASEAN. This ensures that while the physical trade flows efficiently through the northern highways of Kedah, the financial value generated is securely anchored, accounted for, and settled within fully compliant, regulated frameworks.

Suara B. J. Habibie bergetar ketika mengenang bagaimana mimpi besar industri pesawat Indonesia dipatahkan di tengah badai krisis 1998. Dikutip dari Tempo pada Mei 2012, sosok yang dijuluki Mister Crack itu duduk dengan baju koko putih dan selendang peninggalan Ainun di lehernya. 

Tangannya gemetar saat membuka kotak beludru biru berisi medali emas penghargaan dunia penerbangan sipil. Baginya, medali itu bukan sekadar simbol prestasi pribadi, melainkan bukti bahwa Indonesia pernah berdiri sejajar dengan raksasa aviasi dunia. Di balik sorot matanya, ada luka panjang tentang sebuah negeri yang nyaris berhasil terbang tinggi—lalu dipaksa jatuh sebelum menembus awan.

Ketika Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara lahir pada 1976, Habibie memulainya hanya dengan 20 orang. Dua dekade kemudian, perusahaan itu menjelma menjadi simbol kebangkitan teknologi nasional dengan 48 ribu pekerja dan mimpi besar bernama N-250 Gatotkaca. 

Pesawat itu bukan proyek kaleng-kaleng. Ia adalah kebanggaan Asia: pesawat turboprop pertama di kelasnya yang memakai teknologi fly by wire, sistem komputerisasi canggih yang saat itu bahkan belum lazim dipakai banyak negara. Saat N-250 mengudara di Bandung tahun 1996, dunia terpukau. Indonesia seperti sedang menulis takdir baru: dari negara pengimpor teknologi menjadi pencipta teknologi.

Tapi sejarah kadang tak ramah kepada mereka yang terlalu visioner. Krisis moneter 1998 datang bersama syarat-syarat dari International Monetary Fund. Salah satu klausul itu  adalah penghentian subsidi untuk IPTN. 

Artinya sederhana tapi tragis: proyek N-250 harus berhenti, meski tinggal selangkah menuju sertifikasi internasional. Habibie melihat semua yang dibangunnya perlahan dihancurkan atas nama penyelamatan ekonomi. Ironisnya, bertahun-tahun kemudian, maskapai-maskapai Indonesia justru membeli pesawat asing dengan spesifikasi mirip rancangan anak bangsa. Habibie menyaksikan negeri ini mengimpor mimpi yang dulu pernah berhasil mereka ciptakan sendiri.

$XFAB X-FAB Silicon Foundries is the only large independent specialty semiconductor foundry in Europe. 

It does not make AI chips. It does not make memory. It makes the analog and mixed-signal chips that go inside every modern car, every industrial robot, every medical implant, and every power conversion system in the energy transition. 
Six fabs across Germany, France, Malaysia and the United States. 
4,500 employees. 
$870M in 2025 revenues. 
And the single most strategically important semiconductor company Europe has and barely knows it. 

What a specialty foundry actually does, because it is different from everything TSMC does

TSMC makes cutting-edge digital logic chips at 3nm and 5nm. That is not what the world runs on day to day. The chips inside a car power steering module, a pacemaker, a solar inverter, a factory sensor, or an EV battery management system require analog precision, high voltage tolerance and long product lifetimes, not raw transistor density. These chips are built on mature nodes from 180nm down to 110nm and are manufactured by specialty foundries like X-FAB.
The key economics: once a customer designs a chip using X-FAB's process and it enters production, the average product lifetime exceeds 12 years. X-FAB earns a recurring manufacturing fee per wafer for over a decade on each design win. A modern high-end electric vehicle contains up to 180 X-FAB manufactured chips.

The 2025 numbers and 2026 trajectory

FY2025 revenue: 
- $870M, up 6.6% year on year. 
- Q4 2025 alone: $222M, up 18% year on year. The recovery from the automotive and industrial inventory correction is underway.
- Q1 2026: $196M, down 4% year on year on a soft seasonal quarter, but Q1 2026 EBITDA margin of 17.5% and EPS of $0.01 beat the consensus of -$0.01 by 149%. The underlying profitability is recovering faster than revenue.
- Q2 2026 guidance: $190-200M with EBITDA margin of 17-20%. Management confirmed steady recovery trajectory.

The $1 billion capacity expansion is the core of the thesis

Between 2023 and 2025, X-FAB committed $1.0 billion in new capacity across all six fabs. 
This adds approximately 49,000 wafer starts per month to total capacity. The original target was $1.5 billion in annual revenue by 2026. 
The more realistic timeline, given the automotive cycle slowdown, is 2027-2028. But the capacity is being built. The demand is coming. 
And at $1.5 billion in revenue with a 33% EBITDA margin, the company generates $500 million in annual EBITDA versus an enterprise value today of approximately $1.4 billion. 
That is an EV/EBITDA of roughly 2.8x on target economics. 

The European Chips Act is the strategic underwriter

The EU Chips Act deploys €43 billion to rebuild European semiconductor sovereignty. X-FAB's Corbeil-Essonnes fab in France is one of the primary beneficiaries. 
The French government's France 2030 plan and EU sovereign semiconductor strategy explicitly require an independent European specialty foundry at scale. 
X-FAB is the only one that qualifies. Government co-investment, subsidized financing, and strategic support for the French fab expansion are reducing the effective cost and risk of the investment cycle significantly. 
The EU is not funding X-FAB out of charity. It is funding it because without X-FAB, there is no European semiconductor sovereignty in analog and mixed-signal.

The Melexis anchor gives revenue certainty

Melexis, the Belgian automotive chip maker, is X-FAB's largest customer at approximately 35-40% of revenue. Melexis has signed long-term agreements for 2023-2025 at 350nm and 180nm, and a separate LTA for 2024-2027 at 110nm. 
To secure capacity, Melexis prepaid €189 million in advance purchase commitments. Melexis also built its own assembly facility adjacent to X-FAB's Kuching, Malaysia fab to reduce logistics costs. 
This is not a customer relationship. This is a structural interdependency that provides multi-year revenue visibility.

The photonics door is now open

- December 4, 2025: X-FAB and LIGENTEC announced an expanded collaboration on integrated photonics. The partnership specifically brings X-FAB's XPH90 Silicon Photonics (SOI) process and Thin Film Lithium Niobate technology to market jointly. 
Lithium niobate is the next frontier for ultra-high-speed optical modulators, enabling data rates beyond what standard silicon photonics can achieve. 
This puts X-FAB directly inside the AI data center optical interconnect supply chain, alongside the other names in this thesis: $IQE, $SOI, $SIVE.

- December 5, 2025: X-FAB launched XbloX, a design acceleration platform specifically for SiC MOSFETs, enabling power chip designers to bring silicon carbide transistors to market faster using X-FAB's established SiC processes. Expands the SiC customer pipeline beyond existing Tier 1 relationships.

The SiC growth engine is the next re-rating catalyst

SiC revenues in 2025 were approximately $80M. Only 25% of fully electric vehicles currently use SiC inverters, expected to double by 2035. 
X-FAB's Lubbock, Texas fab is the US SiC production center, benefiting from the US CHIPS Act in addition to the EU Chips Act on the European side. STMicroelectronics is investing €5 billion in a new SiC facility in Italy. Onsemi is investing $2 billion in Czech Republic for SiC. The SiC ecosystem is being built at scale. X-FAB is the only independent foundry serving it without captive conflict.
 
The valuation vs peers (EV/Sales)

- X-FAB : 1.5x
- GlobalFoundries : 2.5x
- $TSMC : 8x
X-FAB trades at the steepest discount in the specialty foundry universe despite being the only pure-play European specialty foundry with explicit government support. 

Risks deserve honesty

Net debt will reach approximately $330M by end 2026 as the investment cycle peaks. 
Free cash flow is negative during the capex phase. 
The automotive cycle is still recovering, with Q1 2026 revenue down 4% year on year. 
SiC ramp is running behind the original ambitious schedule. 
Melexis concentration at 35-40% remains a structural risk despite LTA protection. 
Currency risk: revenues predominantly in USD, costs partly in EUR. 

The setup if the thesis is right

$870M revenue growing toward $1.5B. 
$1B in new capacity already committed and partially built. EU Chips Act backing as strategic European semiconductor asset. 
SiC ramp from $80M. 
Photonics door open through LIGENTEC. 
US CHIPS Act benefits on the SiC side. 
$500M in EBITDA on target economics versus $1.4B EV today. 

The market is pricing the investment cycle and the automotive downturn. It is not pricing what comes out the other side.

Not financial advice. Do your own due diligence.

Faktor-faktor ini yang dibaca oleh investor institusional, dan membuat mereka memilih memindahkan modalnya ke tempat lain.

Tapi Bukankah Sentimen Bisa Pengaruhi Pasar?

Ya, sentimen pasar memang nyata dan mempengaruhi pergerakan kurs. Tapi sentimen yang dimaksud adalah sentimen pelaku pasar keuangan global, bukan sentimen yang terbentuk dari timeline Twitter. Mereka membaca laporan ekonomi, proyeksi IMF, dan keputusan kebijakan pemerintah. Bukan thread panjang dari akun anonim.

Dan kalau pun kita terima premis bahwa suasana negatif di publik bisa melemahkan kepercayaan investor, pertanyaannya jadi: apa yang menciptakan suasana negatif itu? Kondisi ekonominya. Bukan kritiknya.

Analoginya begini: kalau ada asap di dapur, yang salah bukan orang yang berteriak ada asap. Yang salah adalah sumber apinya. Menyalahkan yang berteriak bukan solusi. Itu hanya cara supaya dapur tetap terbakar tanpa ada yang ribut.

Negara-negara yang pernah bangkrut akibat krisis ekonomi seperti Argentina, Venezuela, atau Sri Lanka, tidak bangkrut karena warganya terlalu banyak ngomong di sosmed. Mereka bangkrut karena mismanajemen kebijakan yang tidak dikritisi sejak dini, karena alarm diabaikan, serta karena suara peringatan ditekan atau dianggap provokasi.

Kritik bukan racun demokrasi. Kritik adalah sistem peringatan dini.

Menyalahkan orang yang mempertanyakan kebijakan atas akibat dari kebijakan itu sendiri adalah logika yang justru membahayakan.

Aku tidak tahu apakah tweet itu ditulis dengan niat buruk atau cuma frustrasi yang salah arah. Tapi argumennya tetap keliru, serta tanpa data yang mendukung.

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)
Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.
Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Within days, people stopped asking questions. They had already decided he was guilty.

His wife cried everywhere. At church. At family meetings. Even on social media.

People praised her for staying calm through such a painful betrayal.

Meanwhile, her husband watched his reputation collapse.

Friends stopped calling. Relatives stopped visiting. People who had known him for years suddenly looked at him differently.

The pressure became unbearable. Eventually, he moved out.

For seven months, he lived alone.

Seven months of whispers. Seven months of judgment. Seven months of being treated like a thief.

And through it all, nobody stood by him. Not even his own children.

Then something happened.

The bank contacted both of them. There were irregularities in account records and investigators wanted statements.

At first, nobody seemed worried.

The case looked simple. Missing money. One obvious suspect.

But as investigators dug deeper, small details stopped making sense.

Transaction records didn't match earlier claims. Dates didn't line up. Certain transfers raised new questions. Question nobody had been asking.

For the first time in 7 months, attention shifted away from the husband.

Then the truth came out. The ₦12 million had never been stolen.

The husband had never touched a kobo of it. The money had been transferred by someone with full access to the account.

Someone nobody had suspected.

His wife. She had secretly moved the money months earlier.

Not to another man. Not to a business. But to her younger brother.

The same brother she always claimed was struggling financially.

He had used the money for sports betting. And lost almost all of it.

When the truth came out, the entire family was stunned.

The woman who had spent months accusing her husband was the one responsible for the missing money.

She later admitted she never intended for things to get out of control.

She believed her brother would win the money back.

She believed she could quietly replace the funds before anyone noticed. But when everything went wrong, panic took over.

One lie became another. Then another. Until an innocent man lost his home, his reputation, and the trust of his own children.

Eventually, he forgave her. At least publicly. But he never moved back into the house.

When family members asked why, he gave an answer that nobody forgot, "You can recover money, but you can't recover trust."

The money wasn't what destroyed the marriage. It was the fact that an innocent man was abandoned by the people who were supposed to know him best.

If your spouse falsely accused you of stealing ₦12 million and the entire family turned against you for seven months, could you ever truly move on after the truth came out?

Would you stay, leave, or forgive but never trust again? Tell me honestly.
